title: Why a City Dumped 96 Million Black Balls in Its Water
topic: Why a city poured 96 million black balls into its reservoir
mechanism: Sunlight turned the bromide and added chlorine in open reservoirs into bromate, a suspected carcinogen; bottle tests at different depths showed more light meant more bromate and cutting light by about 80 % stopped it, so the city floated cheap black (carbon-black, UV-resistant) balls that block about 95 % of sunlight instead of $300 million covers; less evaporation was a bonus.

beats.hook: You jog past the city reservoir and the water is gone, covered in black balls
beats.story: You figure they are saving water from the sun
beats.rise: You explain it to a tourist like an expert
beats.twist: A lab worker climbs out of a boat holding a sample bottle: evaporation is the bonus, the sun was making a chemical
beats.mechanism: Lab screen BROMATE OVER LIMIT with a 2007 calendar; a bottle labelled SUSPECTED CARCINOGEN; beakers BROMIDE + CHLORINE under a SUNLIGHT lamp turning into BROMATE; a glass tank with bottles on a rope at depths turning red near the surface (MORE / LESS); a LIGHT dimmer to -80% and a NO BROMATE screen; price tags COVERS $300M+ vs BALL 36 CENTS; a light meter SUN BLOCKED 95%; a CARBON BLACK sack in the ball hopper and a UV lamp; the release counter to 96,000,000
beats.ending: Back on the path, the tourist explains it to someone else: it's just to stop evaporation; you facepalm

seed.what: The small boat moored at the far bank and the bottle on a rope (the lab worker's sampling gear)
